title: Transport of normalized pullback composition through coherent realization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and schemes $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On each small pro-etale site set $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$ for $n\ge1$ and $R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $\mathscr D_W=D(\mathscr S(B_{W,\bullet}))$ of whole semilinear systems, with its tensor and geometric inverse image [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. A normalized system has invertible transition adjoints $\alpha^A_{m,n}:q_W^*A_m\to A_n$, where $q_W^*=-\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}$, for all $m\ge n\ge1$, with the identity and quotient cocycles [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. For systems $A,N$ on $W$ and $C$ on $Y$, write $T_W(A,N)_n=A_n\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}N_n$, $F_f(C)_n=Lf_n^*C_n$ for $f:X\to Y$, and $U_W=(B_{W,n}[0])_n$, with the induced whole-system transitions.

Write $\mathcal R_WK=(K\otimes^L_{R_W}B_{W,n})_n$ for coherent reduction [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for total derived limit of the restricted whole system [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Use the canonical adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ and its natural counit $e_A:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WA\to A$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], invertible for normalized $A$ [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]. Let $\widehat T_W,\widehat F_f$ be the actual quotient-complex/Roos completed operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

For finite typed expressions $P$ with input locations and constructors input, coefficient unit, tensor and scheme pullback [def-pur-completed-operation-expressions], let $S_P$ evaluate in $T,F,U$ on normalized inputs, and let $K_P$ evaluate in $\widehat T,\widehat F,\mathcal LU$ on their limits. Define $\beta_P:K_P\to\mathcal L S_P$ recursively by identities at inputs and units, $\beta_{T(P,Q)}=\beta_T(S_P,S_Q)\circ\widehat T(\beta_P,\beta_Q)$ and $\beta_{F_f(P)}=\beta_F(S_P)\circ\widehat F_f(\beta_P)$. Here the primitive maps are those of [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison]: the defining quotient realization followed by $\mathcal L T(e_A,e_N)$ and $\mathcal L F_f(e_C)$, respectively. Put $\gamma_P=e_{S_P}\circ\mathcal R(\beta_P)$.

Let $Z\xrightarrow{h}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ be composable scheme maps and let $C$ be an arbitrary normalized system on $Y$. The finite adjunction-normalized maps
$$a_n: L(f\circ h)_n^*C_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh_n^*Lf_n^*C_n$$
assemble to a natural isomorphism $a:F_{f\circ h}(C)\to F_hF_f(C)$ in $\mathscr D_Z$. Here $a_n$ is the comparison of left adjoints to the canonical direct-image composition identification, not an arbitrarily chosen composition isomorphism [lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition]. Since $\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ is finite and commutative, exact module inverse image computes its derived version termwise [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. On flat-term K-flat representatives the comparison is scalar association: collapsing successive pullbacks multiplies the two scalar factors; the inverse inserts $1$.

The maps in both directions commute with coefficient quotient extension, because reducing before or after multiplication gives the same scalar. For the actual transition of $C$, the coefficient-extension square is composed with the naturality square for $\alpha^C_{m,n}$, using $\tau^C_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}(\alpha^C_{m,n})\circ\eta_{C_m}$; no assumption of canonical-unit input transitions is made. These comparisons are constructed by the whole-system adjunction and scalar-association constructions, so give coherent system maps before taking the limit, with their specified finite adjunction evaluations.

For $P=F_{f\circ h}(C)$ and $Q=F_hF_f(C)$ interpreted as typed expressions, suppose the recursive comparisons $\beta_P,\beta_Q,\gamma_P,\gamma_Q$ are invertible. The actual completed pullback-composition comparison is
$$\widehat a=\beta_Q^{-1}\mathcal L_Z(a)\beta_P,$$
where the quotient-model counits identify its representatives with the above scalar-association maps. Its coherent reduction obeys $\gamma_Q\mathcal R_Z(\widehat a)=a\gamma_P$ by the naturality of $e$. This identifies the completed compositor with the limit of the finite adjunction-normalized whole-system compositor, including its inverse and every actual quotient transition, naturally in $C$.

proof.text: Put $H=F_{f\circ h}$ and write $f_n^*,h_n^*$ for the finite exact module inverse images. Apply [lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition] to $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$. Its comparison is precisely the left-adjoint comparison to the specified direct-image composition, with the canonical constant-section coefficient maps. Exactness from [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] means that applying these functors and this natural isomorphism termwise to any complex computes the unbounded derived functors and their comparison $a_n$. The scalar presentation of the canonical compositor in [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] identifies its inverse $b_n$ with $t\otimes(s\otimes x)\mapsto t\,h_n^\sharp(s)\otimes x$, after the canonical underlying inverse-image composition identification; $a_n$ sends $t\otimes x$ to $t\otimes(1\otimes x)$. Balancing identifies $t h_n^\sharp(s)\otimes(1\otimes x)$ with $t\otimes(s\otimes x)$, so these are inverse maps. The maps have degree zero and commute with the differential termwise. The unit of each scalar-extension adjunction inserts $1$; the displayed $a_n$ carries the composite insertion to the insertion for the composite pullback, which pins the required adjunction normalization.

source.place: Tag 03D8, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; scalar formulas spelled out here

proof.text:
Fix $m\ge n$. Write $\delta_f:q_X^*f_m^*\xrightarrow{\sim}f_n^*q_Y^*$ for $\kappa_f^{-1}$ and similarly $\delta_h,\delta_{fh}$; these are the coefficient-association maps in [lem-pur-normalized-operation-system-models], with the chain formulas of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. They satisfy the natural-transformation equation
$$h_n^*(\delta_f)\,\delta_h(f_m^*(-))\,q_Z^*(a_m)=a_n(q_Y^*(-))\,\delta_{fh}.$$
Here both sides start at $q_Z^*H_m$ and end at $h_n^*f_n^*q_Y^*$. To verify it, invert the compositors and collapse the nested scalar factors as in step 1. Starting with $(t\otimes(s\otimes x))\otimes r$, both routes give $r\bar t\,\overline{h_m^\sharp(s)}\otimes(x\otimes1)$ in $H_n(q_Y^*(-))$, where bars denote the coefficient quotient. Equality follows from $\overline{t h_m^\sharp(s)}=\bar t h_n^\sharp(\bar s)$, since the constant-section maps commute with the quotient ring homomorphism. Balancing and the inverse-image composition identifications are the ones already specified by these cited scalar-association constructions. The inverse square follows by composing with $a_m^{-1}$ and $a_n^{-1}$. Thus this is an equality of chain constructions on the flat-term K-flat models allowed by the system-model lemma, and hence of their derived transformations; no quotient map is assumed flat.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition, with Tag 07A4 scalar-association construction; explicit coefficient-square calculation

proof.text:
Now use the actual adjoint $\alpha=\alpha^C_{m,n}$, not a replacement transition. By [lem-pur-normalized-operation-system-models] the output adjoints are
$$\alpha^P_{m,n}=H_n(\alpha)\delta_{fh},\qquad
\alpha^Q_{m,n}=h_n^*f_n^*(\alpha)\,h_n^*(\delta_f)\,\delta_h(f_m^*C_m).$$
The equation of step 2 followed by naturality of $a_n$ at $\alpha:q_Y^*C_m\to C_n$ gives
$$\alpha^Q_{m,n}\,q_Z^*(a_m)=a_n\,\alpha^P_{m,n}.$$
Under the extension/restriction adjunction of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] this is exactly compatibility with $\tau^C_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}(\alpha)\eta_{C_m}$, and thus with the induced actual transitions of $P,Q$. For the inverse, multiply this equation by $q_Z^*(a_m^{-1})$ and $a_n^{-1}$. Construct the transformation on whole systems by the inverse-image adjunction and module scalar-association transformations of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; that node supplies the system transformations with precisely these finite evaluations. Equivalently the same formulas act termwise on a complex of strict semilinear systems, where the transition square is the preceding scalar calculation followed by naturality for its actual transition chain map. Exactness lets this construction descend to the ordinary derived system category. The two composites with its inverse are identities already in this construction. This constructs $a:P\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ before evaluation, rather than inferring equality of system morphisms from evaluated equalities. The same calculation works for every $m\ge n$; the input cocycle and associative scalar multiplication retain all quotient cocycles.

source.place: Tag 03D8 with the whole-system constructions of lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections; arbitrary-transition calculation using the coefficient square of step 2

proof.text:
Set $D=F_f(C)$. The recursive definitions in the statement specialize to $\beta_P=\beta_{f\circ h}(C)$ and $\beta_Q=\beta_h(D)\widehat F_h(\beta_f(C))$. By [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison], each primitive comparison is the specified quotient realization $r_F$ followed by $\mathcal L F(e)$, and these are natural functor comparisons, including on the actual quotient transitions. Consequently, expressing the nested target in quotient models and applying the inner comparison gives the coherent system arrow $\mathcal R_X(\beta_f(C))$; the outer comparison then applies $F_h(e_D)$. Their composite on the reduced inner argument is $F_h(e_D\mathcal R_X(\beta_f(C)))=F_h(\gamma_{F_f(C)})$. This is exactly the recursive counit identification, with no independently chosen finite identifications. After the source and target have been identified by $\beta_P,\beta_Q$, apply the whole-system compositor of step 3 and then $\mathcal L_Z$. Undoing the target identification constructs the completed compositor as
$$\widehat a=\beta_Q^{-1}\mathcal L_Z(a)\beta_P.$$
All three factors are isomorphisms by the stated hypotheses and step 3. Its inverse is $\beta_P^{-1}\mathcal L_Z(a^{-1})\beta_Q$; direct cancellation verifies both inverse equations. This construction uses the defining quotient-model comparisons for the actual completed functors, so its finite representative maps are the specified scalar-association compositor, transported through the displayed counits.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, used through the primitive quotient/Roos realization comparison; explicit recursive conjugation

proof.text: The representative assertion in step 4 retains the actual limit model as well. On restricted strict towers representing $P,Q$, write $t^P_n,t^Q_n$ for their actual transitions. Step 3 gives $a_n t^P_n=t^Q_n a_{n+1}$. Thus the degreewise product map $A=\prod_n a_n$ obeys $A(1-s_P)=(1-s_Q)A$, component by component. It induces the chain map on $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ by applying $A$ to both cone coordinates; $\prod_n a_n^{-1}$ gives its inverse. On a system resolution the same equations hold after applying that resolution, so this map is carried to $\mathcal L_Z(a)$ by the natural projection-compatible Roos comparison specified in [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison]. The independence and localization compatibility of the actual quotient/Roos models are supplied by [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Therefore the conjugation in step 4 identifies their representatives, inverses and all actual transitions, even when $C$ was not initially a chosen reduction tower. No commutation of a geometric inverse image with an arbitrary product or inverse limit is used.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; functorial cone calculation on actual strict-system maps and the existing quotient-model localization comparison

proof.text:
Finally use counit naturality in the system category, as stated in [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison], at the already constructed $a:P\to Q$. Functoriality and $\beta_Q\widehat a=\mathcal L_Z(a)\beta_P$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
\gamma_Q\mathcal R_Z(\widehat a)
 &=e_Q\mathcal R_Z(\beta_Q\widehat a)
 =e_Q\mathcal R_Z\mathcal L_Z(a)\mathcal R_Z(\beta_P)\\
 &=a e_P\mathcal R_Z(\beta_P)=a\gamma_P.
\end{aligned}$$
For the inverse the same calculation gives $\gamma_P\mathcal R_Z(\widehat a^{-1})=a^{-1}\gamma_Q$. The finite compositor is natural in $C$ by step 1, its whole-system construction is natural by step 3, and the primitive comparisons and their inverses are natural by the cited node; composing them makes $\widehat a$ and this reduction equation natural in $C$. All these equations are obtained in the whole-system category before taking finite evaluations, so include the actual quotient transitions.
